title: Oakridge Retail compatibility runbook + terraform snippets
content:
Audience: Solutions engineering + Oakridge infra + eng-private-deployments.

TL;DR
- Purpose: compatibility checklist, minimal on-prem sizing for Oakridge Retail (edge stores + central analytics), terraform module notes, and a conservative canary/migration plan.
- Recommendation: start with a 3-node inference pool on H100-80GB (or A100-80 if H100 not available), dedicated VPC with private control-plane peering, KMS-backed secrets, and a staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with perf/regression gates.

Context & constraints
- Oakridge will host private inference for customer-facing chat + nightly batch embeddings for product search ranking.
- Regulatory: data must remain within their private VLAN and be encrypted at rest via their KMS.
- Network: stores connect via MPLS to central datacenter; low bandwidth at some sites (50–200 Mbps).
- Ops: limited on-site SREs; prefer automated runbooks and remote-friendly diagnostics.

Assumptions (explicit)
- Model family: Llama-2-13B-ish class (quantized FP16/INT8 recommended).
- Peak concurrent user requests (chat): ~220 RPS across region; P50 token size 30, P95 token size 120.
- Batch embedding jobs: nightly windows, up to 2TB of text processed in 4 hours.
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime for dedicated inference endpoints, p95 latency < 600ms for chat generation (for 512 token max).
- Storage: model artifacts stored on S3-compatible object store accessible from private network.

Minimal capacity sizing (initial)
- Control plane (central): 2 vCPUs, 8GB RAM, 50GB disk (containerized control-plane service, HA pair).
- Inference pool (3x nodes): H100-80GB or A100-80GB recommended, 96 vCPU host, 768GB host RAM, NVMe 1.6TB each for local cache. Estimate throughput: ~700 tokens/s per node (quantized workloads).
- KV cache: memory-resident; allocate ~40GB per node for KV cache for short-context reuse.
- Storage: object store tier + local cache on NVMe for model envs.
- Networking: 25 Gbps NIC recommended for inference nodes (to avoid bottlenecks under burst loads).

Topology (text diagram)
- VPC (Oakridge): private-control-plane subnet <-> inference-pool subnet <-> internal load balancer -> inference nodes
- Optional: edge gateway at each store -> TLS tunnel -> central VPC ingress (for low-latency routing); fallback to hosted API in outage.

Security & compliance notes
- KMS integration: require CMKs in customer KMS; keys used for model-at-rest encryption and ephemeral instance encryption.
- Audit: enable object-store access logs and control-plane audit logging forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Network ACLs: restrict egress to only object-store endpoints and Redwood updater endpoints (list to be provided).

Terraform module notes (practical snippets + gotchas)
- Use existing modules with small adjustments: ri_vpc (v1.3.0) + ri_k8s_node_pool (v2.0.1) + ri_inference_pool (experimental-v0.9).
- Variables to surface for Oakridge: instance_type (h100-type), local_nvme_size_gb, kv_cache_gb, control_plane_cidr, kms_key_arn, s3_endpoint.
- Example:
  module "oakridge_inference_pool" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//ri_inference_pool?ref=experimental-v0.9"
    name = "oakridge-inference"
    count = 3
    instance_type = "nvidia-h100-80gb"
    local_nvme_size_gb = 1600
    kv_cache_gb = 40
    s3_endpoint = "https://s3.oakridge.local"
    kms_key_arn = var.kms_key_arn
  }
- Gotcha: ri_inference_pool's bootstrapscript expects the object-store to allow ranged GETs. Oakridge S3 proxy did not implement ranged reads in a PoC — we must validate.
- Output naming: ensure module outputs model_repo_url and node_private_ips; CI uses these to push model artifacts.

Rolling upgrade & canary plan (stepwise)
1) Preflight (sanity checks)
   - Validate object-store ranged reads, CRL/OCSP for certs, KMS key policy, NTP sync, kernel driver versions for GPU.
   - Run smoke-runner: small workload to validate model load and a trivial prompt correctness test.
2) Canary phase (control plane + 1 node)
   - Deploy control-plane changes (if any) behind feature flag.
   - Enable canary routing: 5% traffic to the new pool. Monitor perf/regressions for 48 hours.
   - Gate: no new model regresses on L1 eval set, p95 latency increase < 15%, and error rate < 0.1%.
3) Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3–5 days with automated rollback on gates.
4) Post-mortem & finalize tags: tag terraform state and publish console rollout notes.

Performance testing checklist (pre-deploy)
- Baseline synthetic generator with token distributions matching Oakridge metrics.
- Soak test: 72h at 70% expected peak, monitor mem, GPU utilization, and GC stalls.
- KV cache hit-rate target: > 45% for chat prefix reuse.
- Failure injection: drop 1 node, ensure router failover within 8s and throttled queue behavior not to exceed p95 target by >2x.

Diagnostics & runbook commands (quick reference)
- Check model load: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://internal-lb/oakridge/v1/models/<model>/status
- Inspect KV cache: rictl cache stats --node <ip>
- GPU health: nvidia-smi | ri-gpu-check (script logs to /var/log/ri/gpu-health.log)
- Flush local cache: rictl cache flush --node <ip> --scope models

Upgrade notes for runtime (important)
- Upgrading runtime from 1.8.x -> 1.9.x requires kernel module bump for the optimized attention kernels (linux >= 5.15). Coordinate with Oakridge infra to schedule node reboots.
- Backwards compatibility: 1.9.x runtime can serve models compiled with 1.8.x but optimal kernels may differ; recommend a single-node canary with representative model.

Risks + mitigations
- Risk: Oakridge S3 proxy lacks ranged GETs -> Mitigation: add a small object proxy lambda in the datacenter that supports ranged reads, or use local persistent model volumes pushed during deployment.
- Risk: MPLS link saturates -> Mitigation: enable local-store-on-demand + aggressive prefix caching, increase KV cache size on nodes at edge.
- Risk: KMS policies too restrictive -> Mitigation: preflight policy delta and a temporary staging key for deployment testing.

Open questions (need Oakridge input)
- Is there a preferred GPU vendor (NVIDIA H100 vs A100) for procurement? Impacts kernel/driver matrix.
- Can Oakridge expose an S3 endpoint with ranged-get and signed URLs for the cluster?
- What is the maintenance window cadence for node reboots? We need at least a 4-hour maintenance window to perform kernel upgrades.
- Does their SIEM accept remote syslog over TLS? Provide endpoint and cert chain.

TODOs (short-term)
- [ ] Run S3 ranged-GET check with Oakridge PoC bucket (Assigned: Diego) — target 2026-03-04
- [ ] Prepare terraform varfile with kms_key_arn placeholder and test drive (Assigned: Priya) — target 2026-03-08
- [ ] Draft customer-facing one-pager summarizing canary plan + rollback (Assigned: Maya) — target 2026-03-10

Appendix: quick performance heuristics
- For Llama-class 13B: estimate ~20–30GB VRAM for tokenizer + KV per active session; plan memory headroom of 1.3x.
- NVMe local model cache reduces model load latency by ~70% vs pulling from S3 on cold start.

Notes / freeform (working area)
- Linnea: check ri_inference_pool bootstrap for Debian vs Rocky images (Oakridge uses RHEL clones). If bootstrap uses apt by default we need yum/dnf variants.
- Ethan: confirm whether instancetype name in their private cloud maps to our terraform variable mapping (we may need a mapping table).
- If customer wants fully air-gapped option, we need to prepare on-prem artifact bundle and a separate offline installer flow (larger offline package, signed).

End of draft.
